title: Finite-level annihilation and internal Hom quotient factorization
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ arbitrary $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Write $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ and $q_n^\mathcal F$ for its cokernel projection, and let $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For integers $0\leq n\leq m$, postcomposition with $q_n^\mathcal F$ annihilates $\mathcal I^n\mathcal H$, and precomposition with $q_m^\mathcal G$ is an isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_m,\mathcal F_n)\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_n)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0882 (lemma-completion-internal-hom, line 6438); the map is left implicit in Stacks and is written out here; the proof there works affine-locally via Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine) and Algebra, Lemma 00MB (lemma-completion-flat) with More on Algebra, Lemma 087R (more-algebra-lemma-pseudo-coherence-and-base-change-ext) for Hom_A(M,N) (x) A^ = Hom_{A^}(M (x) A^, N (x) A^)

proof.text: Let J=I^n. The ideal-module product is the image of the multiplication map J tensor F → F. Its cokernel Q is annihilated by J: tensoring the quotient projection is epi, multiplication is natural, and multiplication into Q is zero after this epi because the cokernel projection kills the product image.

On any open, an O-linear map G → F/I^n F sends a product ax with a in I^m to a times the image of x, which is zero because I^m is contained in I^n when n≤m. Local finite sums generate the ideal product sheaf, so this map kills I^m G and factors uniquely through its cokernel G/I^m G. Restriction to an open preserves cokernels; uniqueness ensures the local factorizations respect restriction and addition and scalar multiplication. Thus the resulting inverse on each open is an inverse of the indicated internal-Hom sheaf map.

Postcomposition sends a local product ah in I^n Hom(G,F) to the map x ↦ a times the class of h(x) in F/I^n F, which is zero by the first step. Locally these products generate the ideal product; hence the composite from that sheaf is zero.
